definition: Logic learning machine (LLM) is a machine learning method based on the generation of intelligible rules.
details: LLM is an efficient implementation of the Switching Neural Network (SNN) paradigm, developed by Marco Muselli, Senior Researcher at the Italian National Research Council CNR-IEIIT in Genoa. LLM has been employed in many different sectors, including the field of medicine (orthopedic patient classification, DNA micro-array analysis and Clinical Decision Support Systems), financial services and supply chain management.

explainer.lead: Logic learning machine is a machine learning method that produces intelligible rules rather than opaque weights. It matters where decisions must be explainable, such as clinical or financial settings.

tiers.eli5: Instead of a black box, it hands you a short list of if-then rules you can read and check.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it when stakeholders need to see the reasoning behind each prediction, and it has been used in medicine, financial services and supply chain management. A pitfall is that rule sets can grow large or brittle on noisy data, so validation matters.
tiers.paperLevel: LLM is an efficient implementation of the Switching Neural Network paradigm, developed by Marco Muselli at the Italian National Research Council CNR-IEIIT in Genoa. Its output is a set of generated rules rather than a continuous model, which bounds how complex relationships can be expressed.

explainer.example: In an orthopaedic patient classification task, the model outputs rules over clinical variables that a clinician can inspect before acting on the recommendation.
